title: Wiped so clean it is as if it never happened
subtitle: The Pardoner who erases sins without leaving a trace
intro: Al-Afuww (العَفُوُّ) means the Pardoner, the One who does not only forgive a sin but wipes it away so completely that no trace of it remains. It is the name the Prophet ﷺ taught us to call on during the most precious nights of the year.

root.sense: Afw is to efface. The Arabs said the wind had done afw to the footprints in the sand when it smoothed them away. The word also carries the sense of what is easy and in excess, given without strain. Al-Afuww erases a sin as wind erases tracks, generously and without difficulty.

row.title: He can wipe the slate clean

knowing: Think of deleting a file on your computer. It goes to the recycle bin, and even after the bin is emptied, a specialist could find a record that it was once there. Formatting the drive is different: nothing remains to be found. {idea}Maghfira covers a sin; afw removes it.{/idea} Many scholars describe afw as the more complete of the two, wiping the sin from the record so that you are never confronted with it.

In the Quran, Afuww almost always comes before Ghafur: Allah is ever Afuww and Ghafur (4:99, 22:60). The order suggests the greater gift first. He does not merely spare you the punishment of a sin; He can erase the sin itself.

He also pairs this name with Al-Qadir, the All-Powerful (4:149). {idea}His pardon is the pardon of One who could take full account and chooses not to.{/idea} That is unlike human pardon, which is often mixed with weakness, or with a memory that brings the wrong back up in the next argument.
seeing: Aishah asked the Prophet ﷺ what she should say if she found Laylat al-Qadr. He taught her: O Allah, You are Afuww, You love to pardon, so pardon me (Jami at-Tirmidhi). On the night when destinies are written, the request he chose was not wealth or ease but this complete erasure.

The closing verse of Surah Al-Baqarah teaches three requests in a row: pardon us, forgive us, have mercy on us (2:286). Erase the sin, cover it from the eyes of others, and keep showing us mercy despite our history. {idea}Believers are meant to be ambitious in what they ask; not just forgive today, but clean the whole plate.{/idea}

His pardon is at work even when we do not notice. Whatever hardship strikes us is due to what our hands have done, yet He pardons much (42:30). The many slips that never came back to us were not forgotten by accident; they were pardoned.
trusting: Some people carry an old sin like a permanent tattoo. They have repented, but they cannot believe they are clean. {trap}Treating yourself as forever stained can quietly become doubt in His pardon.{/trap} Al-Afuww is able to make it as if it never happened. Ask Him for that, and then live like someone who has been asked for nothing more.

Al-Afuww loves to pardon, and He loves it in His servants. {reward}When you let go of someone's offence completely, not bringing it up months later, you become a person who pardons and you place yourself in the way of His pardon.{/reward} Yusuf retold his whole story to his family and left out the well, because he had forgiven his brothers and would not rub it in.
loving: We love people who give us a clean start. Al-Afuww offers something no person can: a start so clean that even the record is wiped. {reward}The heart that tastes this kind of pardon cannot help falling in love with the One who loves to give it.{/reward}
now: It is the last ten nights of Ramadan, 3am, and you are standing in a quiet room with a list of things you wish you had never done. {idea}You do not need a long speech{/idea}: O Allah, You are Afuww, You love to pardon, so pardon me. Say it until you mean it, and trust that He loves to answer it.
old: Even if Allah forgives me, my past will always be a stain I carry around.
new: Al-Afuww can wipe it away as the wind smooths footprints, and He loves to do it.
try: Think of one old grievance you still bring up with someone, and decide today to drop it for good without mentioning it again.

dua.text: O Allah, You are Afuww, You love to pardon, so pardon me. Wipe away what I have done until no trace of it remains, and let me meet You clean.
dua.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught this dua for Laylat al-Qadr (Jami at-Tirmidhi); it is fitting on any night you long for a fresh start.

pairs.why: Afuww Ghafur: He erases the sin and covers its traces, the fullest forgiveness one can hope for (4:99).
Afuww Qadir: He pardons not from weakness but from complete power over every account (4:149).
Al-Ghaffar covers sins again and again; Al-Afuww goes further and wipes them away.

faq.a: Al-Afuww means the Pardoner, the One who erases sins so that no trace remains. The root a-f-w was used by the Arabs for wind wiping footprints from the sand. He pardons generously and without difficulty, and He loves to pardon.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Afuww and Al-Ghafur?
faq.a: Al-Ghafur covers a sin: it is concealed and its punishment withheld. Al-Afuww erases it so that it no longer remains. Many scholars therefore see afw as the more complete level, which is why Afuww often comes before Ghafur in the Quran (4:99).

faq.q: What dua uses the name Al-Afuww?
faq.a: When Aishah asked what to say on Laylat al-Qadr, the Prophet ﷺ taught her: Allahumma innaka Afuwwun tuhibbul afwa fa'fu anni, O Allah, You are the Pardoner, You love to pardon, so pardon me. It is reported in Jami at-Tirmidhi.
